rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 and 3 - the authors develop the WATERMED platform, run a water governance evaluation with the OECD indicator tool, hold three stakeholder workshops and analyse a 43-question Likert questionnaire from 71 participants. Q2: Section 2.1 and Fig. 4 - the platform's first layer integrates IoT sensors, satellite imagery, open data, piezometers and the governance tool and delivers services to farmers, irrigation communities and administrations; Section 3.1.2 notes satellite imagery, piezometric valves and IoT sensors in use in the Spanish pilot; Sections 3.2.1-3.2.3 - 94 % (T<U+00FC>rkiye), 75 % (Spain) and 83 % (Algeria) of respondents said the platform's governance tool helped them learn and they want to use it in future; 91 %/89 % interested in smart-farming technologies. Q5: Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3 and 3.2.1-3.2.3 - results reported separately for three regions (Konya sub-basin, T<U+00FC>rkiye; J<U+00FA>car-Vinalop<U+00F3> basin, Spain; Upper Cheliff plain, Algeria) with different socio-economic contexts. Q6: Section 2.2 and 3.2 - platform tested and stakeholder acceptance reported at basin/sub-basin pilot-area scale with irrigation communities and administrations, not at field scale. Q7: Abstract, Sections 3.1.1-3.1.3 and 3.2 - from the perception analysis the authors state that adoption requires time, training and technical support of farmers and authorities (73 %, 67 % and 72 % say they need technical help) and that investment costs/funding must be addressed; end users require technical and financial support.
rows.notes: Support for the claim is partial: the platform does integrate satellite imagery, but the study's own acceptance evidence (questionnaire) concerns the water governance evaluation tool and the platform generally, not satellite-derived services specifically; no result isolates the remote-sensing component. 'Social cohesion' is the review's label; the study reports stakeholder willingness to use the tool and workshop engagement. Workshops and questionnaire are both stakeholder self-report (one method), so no triangulation. No explicit limitation statement about the survey sample or method; only percentages reported, no dispersion measures.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a platform-design and stakeholder-perception paper; its quantitative results are Likert percentages and traffic-light governance scores for three Mediterranean pilot basins.
